title: Study on the payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area (SPACE) – 2026
content_md:
Understanding the way euro area citizens pay, the evolution of payment habits and the attitudes of consumers towards available payment options is essential to the ECB’s work. As part of our mandate, we are responsible for issuing money, preserving its value and promoting the smooth operation of payment systems.

With this in mind, the ECB has conducted regular surveys on payment attitudes across the euro area since 2016. These surveys have informed the Eurosystem’s cash strategy, comprehensive payments strategy and preparations for the digital euro.

This report presents the fourth edition of the study on the payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area. Ten years after the first comparable survey was conducted, its results show that existing trends have continued, most notably the shift towards digital payments.

For the first time, payment cards have overtaken cash as the most frequently used means of payment at the point of sale, although the gap between the two is marginal. While mobile payments still account for a smaller share of payments, their use is increasing. These are clear signals that consumers are diversifying their payment habits.

Although digital payment options improve convenience, the broader movement towards digital transactions also brings new risks, such as payment fraud. This is an area of concern with 5% of respondents reporting that they have lost money as a result of fraud over the past year. Improving cooperation among authorities and market participants is key to addressing payment fraud, as the tactics used by fraudsters evolve.

At the same time, the high level of perceived acceptance of cash and ease of access to it show that we have a robust cash infrastructure throughout the euro area. We must ensure it remains fit for purpose and caters to citizens’ needs by maintaining its widespread availability and acceptance. This is yet another reason for EU legislators to swiftly adopt the Single Currency Package, which will strengthen the legal tender of cash.

Payment behaviour has changed considerably over the past decade, and this general trend is expected to persist. Yet the preferences of consumers are clear: they still value the ability to choose between different payment options.

The ECB remains committed to preserving people’s freedom to decide how they pay by safeguarding cash while also embracing digital innovation. The work on the next series of euro banknotes and the digital euro reflect this commitment by ensuring that the public will always have the option to pay with central bank money. The level of public interest in cash was shown earlier this year when almost ten million people took part in the ECB’s survey on the design of the new euro banknotes.

As a stable anchor for the payments system, central bank money also provides opportunities for private means of payment to flourish. For example, the digital euro will provide harmonised standards, including for acceptance at the point of sale. Private payment solution providers will be able to use these standards to scale up across the euro area and support a wider range of use cases. This is further proof of the ECB’s commitment to ensuring that the choice of payment method remains in the hands of the consumers.

Piero Cipollone

ECB Executive Board Member

This report presents the key findings of the most recent Study on payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area (SPACE) conducted by the European Central Bank (ECB) in 2026. It compares the new findings with those of the previous SPACE studies (in 2019, 2022 and 2024) and, where relevant, with an earlier ECB Study on the use of cash by households in the euro area (SUCH) conducted in 2016.<sup>\[1\]</sup>

The SPACE 2026 results are summarised below.

- For the first time, cards were used more often than cash at the point of sale (POS) and accounted for 45% of POS transactions in 2026 as compared with 44% for cash. Mobile payments increased in frequency of use, rising from 6% in 2024 to 9% in 2026
- In 2026 euro area consumers made an average of 2.2 payments each day for purchases of goods and services. This is slightly more than in 2024 (2.1 payments on average), but 0.5 payments more than in 2019. Most of the increase took the form of remote payments.<sup>\[2\]</sup>
- Across all payments (POS, remote and person to person or P2P), payment cards were used in 43% of transactions in 2026, up from 39% in 2024. Cash was used in 35% of transactions, down from 40% in 2024.
- Cash retains its strongest position where it has always held it: small value payments and payments between persons. The average card payment fell from €59 in 2019 to €35 in 2026, showing that cards are used for ever-smaller amounts, but cash still dominates payments under €20. In P2P transactions, cash continues to be the method of choice, standing at 44%, ahead of mobile payments (25%), credit transfers (15%) and instant payments (11%).
- Consumer preferences have not changed as much as consumer behaviour. Approximately half (54%) of euro area consumers say that they prefer cards or other cashless methods when paying in a shop, 22% prefer cash and 23% have no clear preference, these figures remaining virtually unchanged since 2022. Cash is valued for its privacy and its role in helping people track spending; cards are valued for convenience and speed. For the majority (62%) of consumers, it is still important to have the option of paying with cash, and 82% indicated, when this question was posed for the first time in 2026, that they consider it important to have the option of paying digitally.
- Access to cash remains satisfactory but is slowly declining. Most euro area consumers (85%) find it fairly or very easy to reach an automated teller machine (ATM) or bank branch, down from 87% in 2024. Of those who tried to withdraw cash in the past year, 19% experienced difficulties, most often because an ATM was closed or temporarily out of service.
- Fraud exposure, broadly speaking, is a concern. In 2026 28% of consumers in the euro area reported experiencing a fraud attempt related to payments and 5% said they actually lost money to payment fraud.
- Cash continues to play a valued role, primarily for mainly small-value POS payments, for P2P payments and as a fallback that a large majority of consumers want to maintain. The median amount of cash held by euro area consumers in their physical wallets in 2026 was €64 (virtually unchanged from €62 in 2024) and 38% of euro area consumers kept extra cash reserves.
- Euro area consumers reported that cash was accepted in 93% of POS transactions in 2026, down from 95% in 2024.

The ways in which consumers in the euro area make payments are constantly evolving. By monitoring payment behaviour and attitudes on a continuous basis, it is possible to capture changes in consumer and market trends.

The SPACE survey does this by, among others, asking people to record in a diary accompanying a questionnaire all the payment transactions they make over one specific day. The results from these diaries are used to estimate the share of different payment instruments used by consumers at the POS,<sup>\[3\]</sup> for remote purchases<sup>\[4\]</sup> and for P2P payments,<sup>\[5\]</sup> including instrument usage breakdowns by demographic. The sample used in the SPACE survey is representative of the euro area adult population and the payment diary data are split equally between different weekdays.

For the 2026 SPACE, a separate P2P diary was introduced into the questionnaire, marking a change in how P2P payments are recorded. Such payments were previously reported as part of the POS and remote payment diaries. The SPACE survey also provides insight into consumers’ payment preferences, their perceived access to cash and digital payments, as well as the acceptance of these payment methods by merchants at the POS.

Building on the previous surveys, SPACE 2026 sought to obtain greater detail in terms of consumers’ views on cash withdrawal difficulties and introduced questions about possible experiences of payment fraud. However, to reduce the response burden for participants, the module on recurring payments (included in the previous studies) was removed from the 2026 survey.

The collection process for the SPACE 2026 data was centralised for the 20 euro area countries surveyed by the ECB, including Bulgaria which joined the euro area in 2026. The German data, on the other hand, were collected by the Deutsche Bundesbank, which applied the same output variables but used a slightly different questionnaire and methodology. Owing to these methodological differences, the German data are not fully comparable with the data from the other countries surveyed. For the Netherlands, SPACE 2026 includes, for the first time, data partially collected through the coordinated SPACE data collection process. In previous waves, these data were collected by De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB), in conjunction with the Dutch Payments Association (DPA), using methodologies differing from those of SPACE. Consequently, caution is advised in comparing some of the results for 2026 for the Netherlands with the results from earlier years.<sup>\[6\]</sup>

Insights into changes in payment behaviour, payment attitudes, access to payment means and acceptance thereof yield important information for the ECB and the Eurosystem. The results will inform further development of the Eurosystem’s payments strategy and cash strategy. They will also make it possible for the ECB, the national central banks and other relevant authorities to implement timely policy measures and continue to ensure equitable access to, and acceptance of, public money. Moreover, the information gathered is helpful in monitoring trends in the use of new means of payment as they gain increasing relevance across the euro area.

Repeating the SPACE survey every two years is therefore important, as are taking steps to further improve its consistency and methodology and continuing to adjust some of the survey questions in line with trends in the retail payment landscape.

Data for SPACE 2026 were collected through a survey of a random sample of the adult population in all euro area countries. The ECB organised the data collection. In addition, the Deutsche Bundesbank collected its own data for Germany and, as for previous SPACE surveys, these were used for the 2026 report. The output variables in the German data are largely harmonised with those used for the other countries. Furthermore, in 2026 the ECB collected the data for the Netherlands for the first time whereas, for previous SPACE waves, DNB, in conjunction with the DPA, had conducted the data collection process. The ECB did, however, again make use of the payment diary data provided by those institutions to complement the centralised data collected for the 2026 wave.

In 2026 the key methodological choices – such as the survey mode, sampling strategy and weighting methodology – were identical to those of the previous SPACE waves for countries included in the centralised data collection process, making the results comparable for most figures. A detailed description of the methodologies used is available in Annex B. This section briefly summarises the methodology.

The data for all countries except Germany were collected using an identical questionnaire (Annex A) translated into the relevant national languages. The market research company Ipsos was responsible for data collection. Approximately half of the interviews were conducted in computer-assisted telephone interviews (CATI) and half in computer-assisted web interviews (CAWI). The CATI sample was drawn using random digit dialling, while the CAWI sample was drawn from non-probabilistic Ipsos online panels. For both samples, quotas for country, age, gender and day of the week were set. The total respondent sample size achieved for the 20 euro area countries surveyed by the ECB was 43,937.

The interview process consisted of three parts: a recruitment interview, the recording period and the main (follow-up) interview. The payment diary was split into modules covering (i) POS payments, (ii) P2P payments and (iii) remote payments. Survey respondents were asked to record their payments in a one-day diary and report the diary data during the main interview.

For the 2026 SPACE, a separate P2P diary was introduced into the questionnaire, marking a change in how P2P payments are recorded (previously they were reported as part of the POS and remote payment diaries). This change has had an impact on the aggregate numbers and values for P2P payments, consequently they are not directly comparable with the data from earlier SPACE waves. It may also have had a moderate impact on the observed distribution of P2P payments by payment instrument.

In addition to the diary, respondents were asked questions about their behaviour and attitudes towards cash and cashless payment instruments in the main interview. Other questions were aimed at providing insight into the perceived advantages of cash or cards, acceptance of payment instruments and attitudes to cash withdrawals, availability of financial products, access to the internet, etc.

SPACE 2026 interviews were conducted in two survey rounds: 48% of interviews were carried out during the first round, which took place between 29 September and 27 November 2025, and the remainder in the second round, between 16 March and 15 May 2026. The survey rounds were spread across different months of the year to capture seasonal patterns in people’s payment behaviour (Table 1). Bulgaria joined the euro area on 1 January 2026; hence the survey was conducted in Bulgaria only in the second survey round.

After the fieldwork period, the data were cleaned, edited and imputed. The sample was weighted to minimise the observable bias of survey estimates and enable solid inferences to be made based on the demographic characteristics. In the weighting procedure, the following survey variables were applied in the calibration process: gender crossed by age, education, employment status, number of household members and region.

In Germany, in 2026 approximately half of the interviews were conducted in CATI and the remainder in CAWI. In previous years the German interviews were collected only in CATI. The German diary data were collected in two survey rounds: between September and November 2025, and between January and May 2026. The German diary data were based on 7,614 respondents, only some of whom were included in the sample of non-diary variables. In contrast to the ECB data collection, German participants were asked to complete a three-day diary. Data for non-diary variables were collected between January and May and were based on 2,006 respondents.

Prior to 2026 the Dutch interviews were conducted mostly in CAWI using non-probabilistic web panels, with only a small share of CATI interviews (2.5% in 2024). This is a different approach from that applied for the SPACE data. Consequently, the data for the Netherlands from previous years are not fully comparable with the data collected in 2026. To enable sound assessment of recent changes in the use of cash at the country level, Charts 7 and 8 on the share of payment instruments used at the POS by country include data from the Dutch national survey.

When interpreting the survey results it is important to acknowledge the benefits and limitations of recording payment behaviour in one-day diaries. Transactions are recorded more comprehensively in diaries covering one day than those for a period of several days (Jonker and Kosse, 2013). However, the degree of uncertainty in any survey data is more pronounced for one-day diaries, especially in seeking to draw conclusions about countries and other sub-groups of a population with small sample sizes.

In the one-day SPACE diary, respondents are invited to record their day-to-day payments. Day-to-day payments consist of payments for purchases of goods and services either at a physical POS or remotely, as well as P2P payments, which are not connected with a purchase of goods and services. Recurring payments, such as rent, mortgage, telephone, utility bills or subscriptions<sup>\[7\]</sup> are not captured in the diary and are not included in the SPACE 2026 survey.

Euro area consumers made an average of 2.2 day-to-day payments each day to purchase goods and services in 2026 (Chart 1, panel a). This is 0.5 payments more than in 2019. In particular, the number of remote payments has increased over this period. Consumers made three times more remote payments in 2026 than in 2019. Remote payments increased steeply during and immediately after the COVID-19 pandemic. However, the increase in remote payments has paused in recent years.

Chart 1, panel b) shows that remote payments to purchase goods and services are higher on average than POS payments in terms of value. The difference between the average value of POS and remote payments was the largest in 2019, when consumers made relatively few remote payments. Since 2019, the average values of POS and remote payments have remained relatively stable. The average payment values for 2019-24 have been adjusted to inflation using the Harmonised index of consumer prices produced by Eurostat.

#### Chart 1

POS and remote payments for purchases of goods and services: average number per day and average value – euro area, 2019-26

On average, consumers in Cyprus (2.36 payments) and Bulgaria (2.22 payments, Chart 2, panel a) made the most POS payments in 2026. The average number of POS payments has increased in all euro area countries between 2019 and 2026, except in Germany, where consumers made fewer daily POS purchases than in any other euro area country (0.97).

There has been a clear increase in the average number of remote payments in all euro area countries between 2019 and 2026 (Chart 2, panel b). On average, consumers in Lithuania (0.80) and Croatia (0.76) made the highest numbers of remote payments in 2026.

#### Chart 2

POS and remote payments for purchases of goods and services: average number per day by country – euro area, 2019 and 2026

Chart 3 shows the differences between demographic groups in the average numbers of POS and remote payments to purchase goods and services. Consumers in urban areas clearly make more POS payments than consumers in rural areas, but also somewhat more remote payments. In addition, remote payments are more frequently made by young consumers (aged 25-39) and by consumers with high education levels.

#### Chart 3

POS and remote payments for purchases of goods and services: average number per day and by demographic – euro area, 2026

Since 2019, the overall shares of payment instruments used for day-to-day payments (POS, P2P and remote payments combined) have changed substantially, both in terms of number and value of transactions. Chart 4 classifies payment instruments into cash; cards (including physical cards used for POS payments and cards for remote payments); e-payment solutions that include mobile payments at the POS and for P2P payments, as well as digital wallets and mobile apps used for remote payments; and other payment methods, such as credit transfers, instant payments (i.e. instant credit transfers)<sup>\[8\]</sup> and direct debit.

Between 2019 and 2026, the share of card payments in total day-to-day payments increased from 25% to 43% in terms of number and from 40% to 44% in terms of value. The share of cash payments decreased from 68% to 35% in terms of number and from 48% to 25% in terms of value. The share of e-payment solutions has increased from very low levels to more than 10%.

#### Chart 4

Payment instruments used for consumers’ day-to-day payments – euro area, 2019-26

POS transactions are defined as payments made at physical locations, for example shops, restaurants and vending machines. In cases where consumers ordered goods online but paid when picking up the goods or paid the courier delivering the goods, these transactions were defined as POS payments.

In 2026 the share of physical card payments in the total number of POS payments was higher (45%) than the share of cash payments (44%, Chart 5). The share of mobile payments<sup>\[9\]</sup> continued to increase and was 9% in 2026, compared with 6% in 2024 and 3% in 2022. In terms of payment value, card payments accounted for more than half of POS transactions (51%).

#### Chart 5

Payment instruments used at the POS – euro area, 2016-26

The volume share of cash payments has decreased faster than its value share. To understand this development, Chart 6 shows the average numbers of payments per consumer and the average values of payments (adjusted for inflation) made at the POS for cash and card payments between 2016 and 2026.

#### Chart 6

POS payments per day and average value of payments with cash and with cards: average number – euro area, 2016-26

The average number of cash payments a consumer makes each day has decreased from 1.28 in 2016 to 0.77 in 2026 (Chart 6, panel a). The average values of cash and card payments have developed differently (Chart 6, panel b). On average, cash payments are lower than card payments. The difference between the average values of cash and card payments declined significantly between 2019 and 2024 but increased again in 2026.

Looking at country-level results, cash was the most frequently used payment method at the POS in ten of the 21 euro area countries surveyed in 2026 (Chart 7). The share of cash payments varied between 18% in the Netherlands and 58% in Slovenia. The total value of physical cash payments exceeded the total value of card payments in seven of the 21 euro area countries surveyed. Data on payments by value reflect some uncertainties and should be interpreted with caution.<sup>\[10\]</sup>

#### Chart 7

Payment instruments used at the POS by country – euro area, 2026

The share of cash payments in POS transactions declined rather significantly in all euro area countries between 2016 and 2026 (Chart 8). The largest decrease has been observed in Cyprus, where the share of cash payments at the POS has declined from 88% in 2016 to 39% in 2026. In Estonia the share of cash payments at the POS has declined by less than 15%, but in Estonia the use of cash was already at a relatively low level in 2016.

#### Chart 8

Cash used at the POS by country: number of payments – euro area, 2016, 2024 and 2026

Chart 9 shows the share of different payment instruments used at the POS in 2026 broken down by the demographic characteristics of the consumer. The use of cash increases with age and is lower for highly educated consumers. In contrast, mobile payments are more frequently used by younger and highly educated consumers. Overall, the differences across the demographic groups are relatively small.

#### Chart 9

Payment instruments used at the POS by demographic – euro area, 2026

SPACE defines remote payments as payments that are not made at the same location as the purchase. This includes online payments, e.g. when shopping in e-commerce and payments initiated at a bank counter or banking terminal. Regular bill payments, such as electricity bills or rent, are not captured in the SPACE diary.

The share of card payments in total remote payments declined between 2019 and 2024, but the latest results for 2026 indicate an increase (Chart 10), whereas the share of e-payment solutions decreased. However, the latter results should be read and interpreted carefully. Between 2019 and 2024, PayPal was a separate answer option<sup>\[11\]</sup> in the questionnaire and for those years was incorporated in Chart 10 under the e-payment solutions group. In 2026 PayPal ceased to be a separate answer category given that it is a method that encompasses several types of payment and overlaps with other answer categories.<sup>\[12\]</sup>

Caution is warranted in general when interpreting trends across payment instruments, particularly in areas where technological developments increasingly blur the distinction between payment initiation channels and underlying payment instruments, such as instant payments (i.e. instant credit transfers).

#### Chart 11

Payment instruments used for remote payments by country – euro area, 2026

P2P payments are payments made to another person that are not connected with the purchase of goods and services, such as payments to family members or friends, pocket money given to children and private donations. They include cash and cashless payments, such as mobile payments<sup>\[13\]</sup> or payments initiated via internet banking.<sup>\[14\]</sup>

Cash was the most frequently used payment method for P2P payments in 2026 (Chart 12), accounting for 44% of all P2P payments, followed by mobile payments (25%). Instant payments are becoming increasingly important in several countries, with their share increasing by 5 percentage points across the euro area compared with 2024.The value share of cash payments was lower (37%) than the volume share.

Cash was used most frequently for P2P payments in Germany (62%) and Bulgaria (58%), and least frequently in Finland (26%), Luxembourg (33%) and Estonia (34%). In Finland (41%), Ireland (35%) and Malta (32%), more than 30% of P2P payments were mobile payments. Instant payment solutions were used most frequently in Lithuania (23%), Luxembourg and Slovenia (both 20%).

Caution is warranted when interpreting trends across payment instruments for P2P payments, particularly in segments where technological developments increasingly blur the distinction between payment initiation channels and underlying payment instruments, such as instant payments (i.e. instant credit transfers).

#### Chart 12

Payment instruments used for P2P payments by country – euro area, 2026

Chart 13 shows the shares of POS and remote payments by value range. While cash payments are still the most frequently used payment method for low-value payments at the POS, consumers are also increasingly using card payments for smaller amounts. The share of card payments increased for payments of less than €5 (24%, up from 21% in 2024) and for payments of between €5 and €10 (39%, up from 32%). In addition, more card payments (46%) than cash payments (44%) were observed for payment values of between €10 and €20. For payments of over €50, the share of card payments has increased only slightly since 2024.

Euro area consumers used e-payment solutions most frequently for low-value remote payments. Overall, the shares of various payment instruments in remote payments were very similar across all value ranges above €5.

#### Chart 13

POS and remote payments by value range and payment instrument – euro area, 2026

In the SPACE payment diary respondents choose between 14 different options when reporting the location of their POS payment. Chart 14 shows the distribution of POS payments by location. Most POS transactions, in terms of both number and value, are made in supermarkets, shops selling day-to-day items and street markets or vendors (55% by number, 50% by value). The share of day-to-day items has increased slightly from 2024. Overall, the structure of the number of POS payments by location has not changed much between 2024 and 2026.

#### Chart 14

POS payments by location – euro area, 2019-26

Chart 15 shows the shares of different payment instruments used in each payment location. Digital payments have increased in most payment locations, and in 2026 cash was the most frequently used payment method only in restaurants, bars and cafés (48%). Consumers are making more digital payments, especially for vending machines (where the combined share of card and mobile payments increased from 39% in 2024 to 54% in 2026) and in cultural and sporting venues (where this share increased from 39% to 58% over the same period). Measured by the value of transactions, cards are the most frequently used payment instrument in all locations.

#### Chart 15

POS payments by location and payment instrument – euro area, 2019, 2024 and 2026

In the SPACE payments diary, respondents choose between 13 different options in reporting the purpose of their remote payment (see footnote 4 in the introduction). Chart 16 shows the distribution of remote payments by purpose. Most remote transactions were made for food and daily supplies (20%) and clothes and sportswear (16%). Measured by the value of payments, household durables (17%) accounted for the largest share.

#### Chart 16

Remote payments by purpose – euro area, 2019, 2022, 2024 and 2026

Chart 17 shows how euro area consumers have responded to the question “How important is it for you to have the option of using cash?”. In spite of the decline in the share of cash payments, having the option of paying with cash remains very important for 30% of the euro area population and fairly important for 32%. These figures have remained stable since 2024, which shows that European citizens continue to see cash as a relevant and important way of paying, despite using it less.

#### Chart 17

The importance of having the option of paying with cash – euro area, 2022-26

In each of the euro area countries, more than half of the respondents considered the option of paying with cash to be very or fairly important (Chart 18). The perceived importance of cash has remained relatively stable since the previous survey in most countries.

#### Chart 18

The importance of having the option of paying with cash by country – euro area, 2026

Chart 19 shows the shares of consumers by demographic group who consider that having the option of paying with cash is very or fairly important. There are almost no differences between male and female preferences. As regards the share of consumers who consider the option of paying with cash to be at least fairly important, the differences between age groups are quite small. Compared with the results from 2024, the importance of cash has increased significantly for younger consumers. People with high education levels give less importance to the option of paying with cash compared with those with low or medium education levels.

#### Chart 19

The importance of having the option of paying with cash by demographic – euro area, 2026

Chart 20 shows how euro area consumers in each country have responded to the question “How important is it for you to have the option of using other payment methods than cash?”. This question was introduced for the first time in the 2026 wave of SPACE. Having the option of paying digitally is very important for 44% of euro area consumers and fairly important for 38% of the respondents. More than 70% of the respondents in each of the euro area countries considered the option to pay with cashless payment instruments very or fairly important. It is more important for respondents with higher education levels compared with other educational backgrounds, and also for respondents in the 25-54 age group.

#### Chart 20

The importance of having the option of paying with cashless payment instruments by country – euro area, 2026

#### Chart 21

The importance of having the option of paying with cashless payment instruments by demographic – euro area, 2026

Chart 22 shows how euro area consumers have answered to the question “If you were offered various payment methods in a shop, what would be your preference?”. After a steady decline from 32% in 2016 to 22% in 2022, a trend that was significantly influenced by the COVID-19 crisis, cash preference remained constant in 2024 and in 2026.

#### Chart 22

Preferred payment instrument in shops – euro area, 2016-26

There are pronounced differences between countries in terms of the preference for paying with cash, card or other cashless payment methods (Chart 23), with Finland having the lowest cash preference (10%) and Austria the highest (39%).

#### Chart 23

Preferred payment instrument in shops by country – euro area, 2026

Looking at payment preferences by demographic (Chart 24), there are almost no differences between male and female behaviour. A similar outcome can be seen for the age group results. A more significant difference can be seen between the attitudes of people with a different education level. In the low and medium education level groups, 25% and 24% of respondents respectively answered that they prefer cash, compared with 18% of respondents in the high education level group.

#### Chart 24

Preferences for cash or cashless payment methods in shops by demographic – euro area, 2026

A follow-up question was asked to all the respondents who stated that they preferred cashless means of payment in order to better understand the type of cashless payment instrument they preferred. In every euro area country, the preferred cashless payment method is physical cards for at least 56% of the respondents (Chart 25).

#### Chart 25

Preferences for cashless payment instruments in shops by country – euro area, 2026

Chart 26 shows information on the perceived key advantages of cash. The results are derived from the responses to the question “For you personally, what are the three most important advantages of cash compared with card payments?”. The respondents could choose up to three of the ten available options.

Euro area consumers perceive the following main advantages of cash payments: cash is anonymous and protects privacy (39%), cash makes one more aware of one’s own expenses (36%) and cash transactions are immediately settled (30%). Just a small share (3%) responded by saying that they do not use cash.

#### Chart 26

Perceived advantages of cash – euro area, 2026

Chart 27 shows information on the perceived main advantages of cards. The results are derived from the responses to the question “For you personally, what are the three most important advantages of card payments compared with cash?”. The respondents could choose up to three of the nine available options.

The most frequently mentioned advantages of card payments were not having to worry about carrying a lot of cash (59%) and the fact that card payments are faster (40%) and easier (35%).

#### Chart 27

Perceived advantages of cards – euro area, 2026

In the euro area, 11% of consumers indicated that they had tried out a new payment instrument in the past year (Chart 28). The share varied between 10% and 15% across countries. Chart 29 illustrates the factors influencing the adoption of new payment instruments. The most frequently mentioned reason by a clear margin was ease of use (47%). Most of the remaining factors received relatively similar levels of support, indicating a broad range of motivations among users.

A similar question was included in the previous SPACE survey, albeit in a hypothetical context. Respondents had been asked to identify the main factors that would persuade them to adopt new payment solutions. In that survey (SPACE 2024), higher security standards were the most frequently cited reason, selected by 37% of respondents in the euro area, followed closely by ease of use at 34%.

#### Chart 28

Share of population who tried a new payment instrument – euro area, 2026

#### Chart 29

Reasons for trying a new payment instrument – euro area, 2026

This chapter provides information on consumers’ access to cash and other payment instruments. It also shows how consumers withdraw cash and what kind of problems they have encountered when trying to withdraw cash from an ATM or at a bank counter.

Chart 30 shows how easy or difficult euro area consumers consider cash withdrawals. The survey question posed is “When you need to withdraw cash, how easy or difficult do you usually find it to get to an ATM or a bank?” 44% of consumers said that access to cash withdrawals was very easy. This is 6 percentage points lower than in 2022 and the perception that access to cash withdrawal is fairly difficult has increased by 4 percentage points over the same time span.

#### Chart 30

Ease of access to cash withdrawals – euro area, 2022-26

Perceived access to cash withdrawals varies across countries. Chart 31 indicates the share of consumers in each euro area country who state that access to cash is very or fairly difficult. Belgium and Malta stand out, with 22% of consumers considering cash difficult to access.

#### Chart 31

Respondents who perceive access to cash withdrawals as fairly difficult or very difficult by country – euro area, 2022-26

For the SPACE one-day payment diary, respondents are also asked to report information on up to two cash withdrawals they have made on that day. Cash withdrawal sources in the questionnaire include bank counters, ATMs, money orders sent to the respondent’s home, banking agents or bank office bus, cash withdrawn in a shop when making a purchase (cashback) or cash withdrawn in a shop without any purchase (cash-in-shop).

In the euro area, ATMs are the most frequently used method of withdrawing cash (Chart 32) and are used for 80% of cash withdrawals. In second place, cashback and bank counters both represent 5%. There is, however, some heterogeneity across the euro area and in a few countries a notable share of respondents withdraw cash at a bank counter or in a post office, such as in the case of Malta (10%), Finland (8%), Italy and Austria (both 7%).

#### Chart 32

Sources of cash withdrawals by country – euro area, 2026

In addition to the diary on payments and cash withdrawals, SPACE respondents are asked more general questions on their withdrawal behaviour and experiences. The results for the question “When you withdraw cash from an ATM or a bank, do you normally combine this with other business, or do you make a special journey from home to the ATM or a bank?” are shown in Chart 33.

At the euro area level, the percentage of respondents indicating that they normally withdrew cash in combination with other activities (e.g. shopping, leisure activities, etc.) was the highest (49%). 26% said they usually make a special journey to withdraw cash, this figure being unchanged from 2024, and 20% stated that they normally combine it with their commute to work or school.

#### Chart 33

Journeys to make cash withdrawals by country – euro area, 2026

The 2026 wave of SPACE introduced new questions to gain a better understanding of the problems that consumers may have in trying to withdraw cash.

Chart 34 shows that 17% of respondents who have tried to withdraw cash at a bank counter and 19% of respondents who have tried to withdraw from an ATM over the past year have experienced difficulties.

#### Chart 34

Withdrawal difficulties at a bank counter and at an ATM by country – euro area, 2026

The 2026 wave of SPACE also introduced the question “What kind of difficulties have you encountered when withdrawing cash …?”. This was posed to all respondents that had experienced difficulties in withdrawing cash from an ATM or at a bank counter over the past year.

Chart 35 shows that the most frequently mentioned difficulties encountered were the closure or temporary unavailability of the nearest machine (62%) for ATM withdrawals and the limited operating hours of counter services for withdrawals at a bank (38%)

#### Chart 35

Types of difficulty with withdrawals at an ATM and a bank counter – euro area, 2026

Chart 36 shows the frequency at which consumers reported having to pay fees, which highlights perceptions of the different fee structures across countries. In the euro area, 55% of respondents reported not having to pay a fee at all, a small decline from the 57% observed in 2024.

#### Chart 36

Perceived frequency of fees for cash withdrawals with an ATM by country – euro area, 2026

To understand how consumers feel when they are charged a fee, the SPACE questionnaire included the following question: “What did you do the last time you were asked for a fee when you went to withdraw money at an ATM?” and provided four predefined answer options (Chart 37).

At the euro area level, 58% of respondents indicated that they paid the fee either because there was no other option for withdrawing cash or because the fee was acceptable. On the other hand, 21% decided to cancel the operation and 12% decided not to withdraw cash at all.

In all euro area countries other than Spain, the most frequently reported response was that the fee was paid because there was no other option for withdrawing cash. The share of respondents selecting this option was at least 40% in Bulgaria, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg and Finland. In Spain, the most frequently reported response was to cancel the operation, closely followed by paying the fee because there was no other option for withdrawing cash.

#### Chart 37

Reaction to ATM fees for cash withdrawals by country – euro area, 2026

Chart 38, panel a) shows that, on average, the share of respondents in the euro area reporting ownership of a payment account increased from 96% in 2024 to 98% in 2026. Chart 38, panel b) indicates that the share of respondents who own a payment card increased from 92% in 2024 to 96% in 2026.

The highest percentage of consumers who own a payment card was recorded in Germany (99%) and France, Finland and Luxembourg (98%). Compared with 2024, Lithuania has seen the most significant increase in payment card ownership, with an 11 percentage point rise.

#### Chart 38

Consumers who have a payment account or card by country – euro area, 2024-26

There is usually a direct link between access to payment accounts and payment cards. It is possible, however, to have the one without the other, although the payment methods available may be restricted in such cases. Looking at the euro area, ownership of bank accounts and payment cards is highly homogeneous, with rates exceeding 90% across most demographic categories (Chart 39).

#### Chart 39

Consumers who have a payment account or card by demographic – euro area, 2026

Of all euro area consumers who own a payment card 47% have stored at least one payment card in a digital wallet, such as Apple or Google Pay (Chart 40). The share varies across countries, from 40% in Germany to 63% in Ireland.

#### Chart 40

Consumers owning a payment card who have stored at least one card in a digital wallet by country – euro area, 2026

The share of respondents who report that they do not need assistance when paying online, with a card or with a mobile phone, has remained identical, at 83% (Chart 41), for the euro area since 2024.

In the 2026 wave, respondents were asked for the first time to indicate whether they have a disability or are in a vulnerable position<sup>\[15\]</sup>, which is the case for 14.6% of all respondents. On average, those in the euro area reporting a disability or vulnerability are more likely to require assistance when making online payments (13%) than those who did not (8%), as shown in Chart 42.

#### Chart 41

Assistance with digital payments by country – euro area, 2026

#### Chart 42

People in a vulnerable position and those in need of assistance by country – euro area, 2026

Respondents were asked whether they owned crypto-assets, including stablecoins. Chart 43 shows that the share of respondents in the euro area who own crypto-assets or stablecoins increased by 1 percentage point between 2024 and 2026. The country with the highest share of crypto-asset ownership in 2026 is Slovenia, with 17%.

#### Chart 43

Possession of crypto-assets by country – euro area, 2024-26

Respondents who reported that they own crypto-assets were subsequently asked whether they held them for payment, investment or both purposes. Despite variations, the results indicate a clear preference for using crypto-assets only as a means of investment (Chart 44).<sup>\[16\]</sup>

#### Chart 44

Use of crypto-assets by purpose and by country – euro area, 2026

In the SPACE payment diary, respondents were asked to report for each POS payment not made using cash, whether cash would also have been accepted. The perceived cash acceptance rates (Chart 45) indicate the share of POS transactions that were either paid with cash or where the respondent indicated that cash would have been accepted.

Cash is accepted in most POS transactions (93%) performed in all euro area countries, as against 95% in 2024. Compared with 2024, respondents from all countries included in the survey reported no variations or slightly negative changes in acceptance.

#### Chart 45

Perceived acceptance rates of cash in POS transactions by country – euro area, 2024-26

Similarly, SPACE respondents are asked to indicate for each POS payment paid with cash, whether other payment methods, such as card or mobile payments, would also have been accepted. The perceived acceptance rates of cashless payments (Chart 46) indicate the share of POS transactions that were either paid with payment methods other than cash or where the respondent indicated that other cashless payment methods would have been accepted.

SPACE data show that for most POS payments in the euro area, cashless payment methods are accepted (91%). Compared with 2024, the acceptance rates of cashless payments increased by 3 percentage points in 2026.

#### Chart 46

Perceived acceptance rates for cashless payments in POS transactions by country – euro area, 2024-26

After reporting the information from the payment diary, SPACE respondents were asked, in a separate question, to reflect on all the transactions they had conducted at physical locations over the past month and to indicate whether the merchant or payee had always offered the payment method they would prefer to use. The findings indicate that 74% of consumers were always able to use their desired payment method (Chart 47), representing an increase compared with 2024.

In all euro area countries, at least 12% of consumers had experienced non-acceptance of mobile or card payments, irrespective of the amount, at least once in the month preceding the survey (Chart 48). In addition, 7% of euro area consumers said that cards and mobile payments were not accepted below a certain amount. Furthermore, 6% of respondents in the euro area reported that cash had not been accepted at least once in the month preceding the interview, that percentage being the same as in 2024.

#### Chart 48

Experiences of payment acceptance – euro area, 2026

This section looks at the cash holdings of individuals. SPACE collects data on both readily available cash, such as banknotes and coins stored in physical wallets, pockets or bags, as well as cash reserves kept elsewhere.

The SPACE questionnaire collects information on readily available cash by asking respondents the following: “How much cash did you have at the beginning of *diary day*?”. This question is posed at the beginning of the payment diary module and relates solely to cash that is readily available, and not the respondents’ cash reserves<sup>\[17\]</sup>.

As shown in Chart 49, individuals in the euro area had a median amount of €64 readily available to them, this figure being similar to that observed in 2024 (€62).<sup>\[18\]</sup> The reported median cash amounts varied across different countries. Luxembourg had the highest median cash holdings (€100), whereas France and Finland recorded the lowest (€52 and €50 respectively).

#### Chart 49

Median amount of cash in wallet at the beginning of the day by country – euro area, 2026

To collect information on cash reserves the following question was posed in the SPACE questionnaire: “Some people like to keep cash at home or somewhere else for various reasons, e.g. to top up their wallet, as a precautionary reserve or as an alternative way of saving. Do you personally keep extra cash that is not in your wallet, purse, or pocket?”. The results show that 38% of respondents kept cash reserves in 2026 (Chart 50), compared with 35% in 2024.

The highest share of respondents maintaining extra cash as a store of value was to be found in Slovakia (58%). France and Belgium reported the lowest percentages (28% and 29% respectively).

#### Chart 50

Consumers keeping extra cash reserves by country – euro area, 2026

The respondents were surveyed for the first time about their experiences with fraud attempts and whether those attempts resulted in financial loss. Chart 51 shows the country-specific results for these questions. The share of euro area respondents reporting fraud attempts is, on average, 28%, with 5% of all consumers (or 18% of consumers having experienced a fraud attempt) reporting that they had lost money to fraudsters.

#### Chart 51

Fraud attempts experienced and those resulting in fraud – euro area, 2026

Higher fraud attempt rates are observed in Ireland (45%), Latvia (39%) and Lithuania (38%). However, these differences may partly reflect variations in how respondents interpret and identify fraud attempts. For example, some respondents might have considered only concrete actions, such as direct communication attempts, while others may have included spam messages received by email, SMS or other messaging apps, which are also classified as fraud attempts.

#### Chart 52

Instrument used in fraudulent payments – euro area, 2026

The respondents who reported having actually lost money cited (instant) credit transfers<sup>\[19\]</sup> and physical card payments as the most commonly used instruments to execute the fraud.

#### Chart 53

Method used in fraudulent payments – euro area, 2026

When asked about the method of fraud experienced, the answer most frequently reported was through encountering a fake website. The second most frequent response was via SMS (or messaging apps), followed by fake emails. Nevertheless, there may be some overlap between these three categories. Typically, accessing a fake website requires clicking a link received in an email or some form of messaging. These types of fraud often involve social engineering techniques, where fraudsters manipulate individuals into taking specific actions (authorised push-payment fraud).

3. POS payments include purchases of goods or services at supermarkets, shops selling day-to-day items, street or market selling points, shops selling durable goods, restaurants, bars, cafés, petrol stations, vending and ticketing machines, pick-up stations, cultural, sporting and entertainment venues, offices of public authorities, hotels or the like, including services provided outside the home (e.g. hairdressing, dry cleaning, bicycle repair), inside and around the home (e.g. cleaning, babysitting), and at other physical locations.

Remote payments were called online payments in earlier SPACE reports.
5. P2P payments are private transactions between individuals that are not connected with the purchase of goods and services, e.g. charitable donations and other payments to private persons, such as pocket money or gifts. P2P payments can be either physical or remote.

9. Mobile payments at the POS are defined as payments via smartphones, smartwatches, smartrings and any other mobile or wearable devices, and can be based on cards in a wallet, instant payments, other mobile apps or crypto-assets.

In the Chart, the categories digital wallets and other mobile apps are included in E-payment solutions, while buy-now-pay-later falls into the category Other.

title: Card payments edge past cash in shops; euro area consumers want both
content_md:
- PRESS RELEASE

25 November 2026

- Physical cards account for 45% of payments in shops, compared with 44% for cash
- Cash remains especially important for small value payments and payments between individuals
- Ability to pay digitally and with cash are both important to consumers

The European Central Bank (ECB) today published its latest study on the payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area (SPACE). The results show that consumers are increasingly using digital means of payment, while cash continues to play an important role.

For the first time since comparable data were collected in 2016,<sup>\[1\]</sup> cards were used more often than cash at physical locations, such as shops. In 2026 cards accounted for 45% of transactions, compared with 44% for cash. Mobile payments increased to 9%, from 6% in 2024.

While payment practices are changing, consumers’ own preferences remain stable. When paying in a shop, 54% preferred cards or other cashless methods, 22% preferred cash and 23% had no clear preference.

A large majority of respondents attach importance to retaining a choice of payment methods. For 82% of euro area consumers, it is important to have the option to pay digitally, while 62% value the option of paying with cash. Only 3% reported never using cash.

“Digital means of payment are becoming more important in day-to-day transactions, but choice is what really matters for Europeans,” said Piero Cipollone, member of the ECB’s Executive Board. “The ECB will continue to ensure citizens have the freedom to choose how to pay, by safeguarding cash while preparing for the possible issuance of its digital equivalent, the digital euro.”

Most consumers continue to find it easy to access cash, although the share declined to 85%, from 87% in 2024. Among those who had tried to withdraw cash from an ATM during the previous year, 19% experienced difficulties. In all euro area countries, at least 12% of consumers experienced non-acceptance of mobile or card payments at least once in the month preceding the survey.

The survey covered 51,551 respondents across the euro area. Data were collected in two rounds: the first between 29 September and 27 November 2025, and the second between 16 March and 15 May 2026.

**For media queries, please contact Alessandro Speciale, tel.: +49 172 1670791.**

1. Previous editions of the SPACE study were published in 2019, 2022 and 2024. In 2016 the ECB published a study on the use of cash by households in the euro area (SUCH).

title: Gold Trades Near 15-Month Low as Federal Reserve Rate Hike Expectations Weigh on Prices
content_md:
Gold prices declined on Wednesday, remaining close to their lowest levels in 15 months as expectations of further monetary tightening by the US Federal Reserve and a stronger dollar continued to weigh on precious metals.

Investors remained cautious ahead of the publication of key US inflation figures later in the session, which could influence expectations for the central bank's December interest rate decision.

At 06:22 GMT, spot gold was down 1% at $3,522.68 per ounce, while US gold futures declined 1.1% to $3,521.60.

The precious metal has struggled to regain ground following last week's sharp sell-off, which pushed prices to their lowest level since early September 2025.

#### Markets Price in December Federal Reserve Rate Increase

Expectations of higher US interest rates remain a significant source of pressure on gold, which does not generate interest income.

According to CME's FedWatch tool, financial markets were pricing in a 96.4% probability of a 25-basis-point interest rate increase at the Federal Reserve's December meeting.

The probability of a larger increase of 50 basis points stood at 3.6%.

Attention is now focused on the upcoming US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation measure.

The figures, scheduled for release later on Wednesday, will represent the final major inflation report ahead of the central bank's last monetary policy meeting of the year on 8–9 December.

#### Stronger US Economic Indicators Support Monetary Tightening Expectations

Recent US economic data have reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve could continue raising interest rates.

US consumer confidence increased more than anticipated in November, reaching its highest level in nearly two years.

The improvement reflected greater optimism surrounding labour market conditions and the broader economic outlook following this month's midterm elections.

New York Federal Reserve President John Williams indicated that persistent inflation continued to warrant tighter monetary policy, although the pace of future interest rate increases would depend on incoming economic data.

Meanwhile, the US dollar has recently traded near a 19-month high, adding further pressure to precious metal prices.

A stronger dollar increases the cost of purchasing gold for investors holding other currencies, potentially reducing international demand.

#### Silver, Platinum and Copper Also Decline

Weakness extended across other precious and industrial metals on Wednesday.

Spot silver fell 1.3% to $40.38 per ounce, while platinum declined 1.3% to $1,258.44 per ounce.

Benchmark copper futures traded on the London Metal Exchange fell 0.7% to $11,762.33 per tonne.

US copper futures recorded a larger decline of 1.5%, trading at $5.32 per pound.

title: Oil Prices Extend Declines as Rising Supply Pressures Brent and WTI Despite Hormuz Tensions
content_md:
Crude oil prices continued to fall on Wednesday as signs of increasing supply and weakening demand in refined petroleum markets outweighed concerns about renewed attacks on commercial shipping near the Strait of Hormuz.

At 03:53 GMT, Brent crude futures were trading 1.4% lower at $90.12 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures declined 1.6% to $80.73 per barrel.

WTI had gained 2.4% during the previous trading session, while Brent had settled above $91 per barrel.

#### Shipping Disruptions Continue as Iran Threatens Further Restrictions

Concerns surrounding the security of commercial shipping in the Middle East intensified following reports of additional incidents involving vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency reported further attacks involving three vessels, while Iranian news agency Fars separately reported another incident involving a tanker on Tuesday.

Tehran has threatened to strengthen its control over the strategic waterway until its demands are addressed, including the removal of the US blockade on Iranian ports, sanctions relief and the release of frozen Iranian assets.

US Vice President JD Vance met Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani to discuss regional developments. However, significant differences remain between Washington and Tehran in ongoing negotiations.

NBC also reported that US officials were considering potential action against senior Iranian leaders.

Regional tensions extended to Saudi Arabia following a reported Houthi attack in Riyadh that injured two Saudi nationals and nine foreign residents.

#### Increasing Crude Supplies Offset Geopolitical Concerns

Despite renewed hostilities in the Middle East, crude oil exports from the Persian Gulf have increased over recent months.

A closely monitored price spread for Dubai crude, the regional oil benchmark, moved into a bearish market structure this week, suggesting that immediate supply availability was exceeding near-term demand.

However, analysts at ANZ cautioned that the apparent improvement in supply conditions could obscure significant vulnerabilities within the global oil market.

Crude exports from the Persian Gulf remain substantially restricted, with oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz operating at just 49% of normal levels.

Although inventories and petroleum product availability have improved somewhat, ANZ analysts noted that global stockpiles remain exceptionally low and spare production capacity is almost entirely exhausted.

title: Thai retail giant CP to shut down all 7-Eleven stores in Cambodia
description: All 23 remaining 7-Eleven stores in Cambodia will shut down as Thailand’s largest retailer CP All plans to cease the chain’s operations in the country following boycotts triggered by border tensions.
content_md:
"Such cessation is in accordance with the mutually agreed terms between the company and the owner of the 7-Eleven trademark rights," CP All said in a filing Tuesday with the Stock Exchange of Thailand, adding that the stores will close by Dec. 25.

CP All is a subsidiary of Thai conglomerate CP Group, controlled by Thailand’s richest man Dhanin Chearavanont.

The number of 7-Eleven stores in Cambodia has fallen by 80% since last year, from 112 to 23 in September, as reported by *KiriPost.*

| The 7-Eleven shop logo is seen in Ohio, United States, on August 4, 2026. Photo by NurPhoto via AFP |

The decline in store number brought down earnings. Net profit in the third quarter fell 20% year-on-year to 5.9 billion baht ($172.4 million). Quarterly revenue rose 4.5% to 262 billion baht.

The group’s Cambodian businesses include Makro (Cambodia), which operates Makro hypermarkets, and Indoguna (Cambodia), which imports and trades in food-related products.

The group also owns ALL IM-EX and Proservice Co, which produces ready-to-eat food for convenience stores and distributes goods.

In 2020, CP All signed a master franchise agreement with U.S.-based 7-Eleven Inc. to bring the global chain to Cambodia. The first store opened in 2021.

The group’s annual report for the financial year ended Dec. 31, 2025 showed that the franchise agreement with Japanese-owned 7-Eleven had a 30-year term with an option for two 20-year extensions.

The agreement requires the Cambodian subsidiary to pay the trademark owner a monthly fee based on an undisclosed percentage of the stores’ total sales and other income.

In its latest quarterly results, CP All discussed plans to add 700 stores this year in Thailand and Laos. The group has more than 16,200 stores in Thailand and 39 in Laos. In Cambodia, the company said it had "refined its strategy to suit changing operational circumstances."

The Thai group is the exclusive operator and franchisor of 7-Eleven in Thailand, Cambodia and Laos under a 1988 licensing agreement with the chain’s parent company.

Cambodians welcomed 7-Eleven when it entered the market, but sales are believed to have fallen as a boycott of Thai products gained momentum. It was driven largely by protests from both countries that continued despite a ceasefire and a peace agreement the two sides signed after two clashes in 2025.

Alongside a widespread consumer boycott, the prolonged border closure made it harder for 7-Eleven stores in Cambodia to replenish stocks because many of their products came from Thailand, according to the *Bangkok Post.*

title: Đề nghị 13 tỉnh, thành phố đẩy nhanh tiến độ hoàn thiện dữ liệu đất đai
description: Bộ Nông nghiệp và Môi trường đề nghị 13 tỉnh, thành phố tập trung chỉ đạo, đẩy nhanh tiến độ xây dựng, hoàn thiện cơ sở dữ liệu đất đai, bảo đảm thực hiện các mục tiêu, nhiệm vụ theo kế hoạch được giao.
content_md:
Bộ Nông nghiệp và Môi trường đề nghị 13 tỉnh, thành phố tập trung chỉ đạo, đẩy nhanh tiến độ xây dựng, hoàn thiện cơ sở dữ liệu đất đai, bảo đảm thực hiện các mục tiêu, nhiệm vụ theo kế hoạch được giao.

Bộ Nông nghiệp và Môi trường vừa ban hành Công văn số 13477/BNNMT-QLĐĐ gửi Chủ tịch UBND 13 tỉnh, thành phố gồm: Hà Nội, Cao Bằng, Tuyên Quang, Điện Biên, Sơn La, Lạng Sơn, Phú Thọ, Hưng Yên, Thanh Hóa, Quảng Ngãi, Lâm Đồng, Đắk Lắk và An Giang; yêu cầu tập trung chỉ đạo, đẩy nhanh tiến độ xây dựng, hoàn thiện cơ sở dữ liệu đất đai, bảo đảm thực hiện các mục tiêu, nhiệm vụ theo kế hoạch được giao.

Theo Bộ Nông nghiệp và Môi trường, tính đến ngày 23/11, cả nước đã xây dựng và đồng bộ dữ liệu của 74,6 triệu trong tổng số 105,3 triệu thửa đất. Trong đó, 62,8 triệu thửa đất có dữ liệu bảo đảm tiêu chí Nhóm I "đúng - đủ - sạch - sống"; 11,8 triệu thửa đất thuộc Nhóm II cần tiếp tục hoàn thiện.

Việc kết nối, chia sẻ và khai thác dữ liệu đất đai từng bước phục vụ hiệu quả công tác quản lý nhà nước, giải quyết thủ tục hành chính và cung cấp dịch vụ công. Đáng chú ý, hơn 2 triệu hồ sơ giải quyết thủ tục hành chính của các bộ, ngành, địa phương đã sử dụng dữ liệu đất đai thay thế thành phần hồ sơ giấy; hơn 11 triệu lượt yêu cầu khai thác, sử dụng dữ liệu được thực hiện.

Bên cạnh đó, 462 cơ quan thuế cơ sở đã sử dụng dữ liệu đất đai để xác định nghĩa vụ tài chính khi giao đất, cho thuê đất và thu thuế sử dụng đất phi nông nghiệp. Bộ Công an đã đồng bộ 54,4 triệu dữ liệu đất đai về Trung tâm dữ liệu quốc gia, tích hợp 31,4 triệu Giấy chứng nhận trên ứng dụng VNeID; hơn 20.000 hồ sơ đăng ký thường trú, tạm trú được xử lý thông qua kết nối, khai thác thông tin từ cơ sở dữ liệu đất đai.

Mặc dù đạt được những kết quả tích cực, qua theo dõi, đánh giá, Bộ Nông nghiệp và Môi trường xác định còn 5 tỉnh có nguy cơ không hoàn thành chỉ tiêu năm 2026 theo Quyết định số 88/QĐ-BCĐCP ngày 29/7/2026 của Ban Chỉ đạo Chính phủ.

Cụ thể, Tuyên Quang đạt 65%, Lạng Sơn đạt 67%, Lâm Đồng đạt 68%, An Giang đạt 70% và Sơn La đạt 72%. Đây là những địa phương cần tập trung chỉ đạo, huy động nguồn lực, nhân lực để đẩy nhanh việc chuẩn hóa, đối soát, bổ sung, làm sạch dữ liệu đất đai đã có.

Bộ yêu cầu các tỉnh khẩn trương rà soát, đánh giá chính xác khối lượng và tiến độ thực hiện; xác định rõ nguyên nhân chậm, khó khăn, vướng mắc cũng như trách nhiệm của các cơ quan, đơn vị liên quan. Đồng thời, tập trung hoàn thiện dữ liệu theo tiêu chí "đúng - đủ - sạch - sống", bảo đảm đồng bộ những dữ liệu đủ điều kiện vào cơ sở dữ liệu quốc gia về đất đai tại Bộ Nông nghiệp và Môi trường, phục vụ kết nối, chia sẻ với Trung tâm dữ liệu quốc gia và Cơ sở dữ liệu quốc gia về dân cư.

Các địa phương phải hoàn thành tối thiểu 80% số thửa đất đã có dữ liệu được chuẩn hóa, đối soát, làm sạch và đủ điều kiện đồng bộ trước ngày 30/11/2026. Kết quả thực hiện phải báo cáo Bộ Nông nghiệp và Môi trường trước ngày 3/12/2026.

#### 10 địa phương còn khối lượng lớn nhiệm vụ năm 2027

Đối với nhiệm vụ năm 2027, Bộ Nông nghiệp và Môi trường chỉ rõ 10 tỉnh, thành phố còn khối lượng lớn thửa đất phải thực hiện đo đạc, lập bản đồ địa chính, lập hồ sơ địa chính, đăng ký đất đai và xây dựng cơ sở dữ liệu.

Trong đó, Phú Thọ còn 5,5 triệu thửa đất; Thanh Hóa và Quảng Ngãi cùng còn 2,9 triệu thửa; Tuyên Quang 2,2 triệu thửa; Lâm Đồng 2,1 triệu thửa; Hà Nội 1,7 triệu thửa; Điện Biên 1,5 triệu thửa; Hưng Yên 1,3 triệu thửa; Cao Bằng và Đắk Lắk cùng 1,2 triệu thửa.

Bộ yêu cầu các địa phương khẩn trương rà soát toàn bộ khối lượng công việc còn lại, xây dựng kế hoạch triển khai cụ thể, xác định rõ khối lượng, tiến độ, nguồn lực, kinh phí và trách nhiệm của từng cơ quan, đơn vị, bảo đảm hoàn thành mục tiêu trong năm 2027.

Cùng với đó, chủ động bố trí nguồn lực, thực hiện các thủ tục đầu tư, lựa chọn đơn vị thực hiện theo quy định; tổ chức đồng bộ công tác đo đạc, lập bản đồ địa chính, đăng ký đất đai, lập hồ sơ địa chính và xây dựng cơ sở dữ liệu đất đai, bảo đảm chất lượng, tiến độ, tránh trùng lặp, lãng phí. Quá trình triển khai cần lồng ghép các hoạt động theo quy định tại Thông tư số 19/2026/TT-BNNMT ngày 30/3/2026 của Bộ Nông nghiệp và Môi trường.

Bộ cũng đề nghị Chủ tịch UBND các tỉnh, thành phố trực tiếp quan tâm chỉ đạo, phân công rõ trách nhiệm của các sở, ngành, đơn vị và chính quyền cấp xã; thường xuyên kiểm tra, đôn đốc, kịp thời tháo gỡ khó khăn, vướng mắc.

Đối với 10 địa phương còn khối lượng lớn nhiệm vụ năm 2027, kế hoạch triển khai phải được hoàn thiện và gửi về Bộ Nông nghiệp và Môi trường trước ngày 25/12/2026 để tổng hợp, theo dõi, đôn đốc.

Cục Quản lý đất đai được giao chủ trì, phối hợp với các đơn vị liên quan theo dõi, hướng dẫn, đôn đốc, tổng hợp kết quả thực hiện; kịp thời báo cáo Lãnh đạo Bộ những khó khăn, vướng mắc vượt thẩm quyền để xem xét, xử lý.

title: Trung Quốc báo tin vui đến toàn thế giới
description: Các nhà máy lọc dầu Trung Quốc đang tăng mạnh mua dầu thô khi giá và cước vận chuyển cùng hạ nhiệt.
content_md:
Các nhà máy lọc dầu Trung Quốc đang tăng mạnh mua dầu thô khi giá và cước vận chuyển cùng hạ nhiệt.

Các nhà máy lọc dầu Trung Quốc đang tranh thủ đợt giảm giá dầu gần đây để tăng nhập khẩu và bổ sung kho dự trữ. Động thái mua vào đặc biệt rõ nét ở Tây Phi. Tập đoàn dầu khí Sinopec của Trung Quốc đã mua khoảng 20 triệu thùng dầu thô từ khu vực này kể từ đầu tháng 11, với các lô hàng dự kiến được bốc lên tàu trong tháng 12.

Quy mô này đáng chú ý khi thông thường, toàn bộ khách hàng Trung Quốc chỉ mua trung bình khoảng 20-25 triệu thùng dầu Tây Phi mỗi tháng. Nói cách khác, lượng dầu Sinopec mua từ đầu tháng đã gần bằng nhu cầu hàng tháng của tất cả khách hàng Trung Quốc cộng lại trong điều kiện bình thường.

Không chỉ Tây Phi, các nhà máy lọc dầu nước này còn tăng mua dầu từ Trung Đông và Brazil khi giá trở nên hấp dẫn hơn. Theo các thương nhân, một số loại dầu của Saudi Arabia và Iraq giao ngay tới Đông Á hiện chỉ được chào bán với mức cộng khoảng 2-3 USD/thùng so với giá dầu chuẩn Dubai. Mức này thấp hơn đáng kể so với cuối tháng 10, khi dầu Basrah của Iraq từng có mức cộng khoảng 12 USD mỗi thùng.

Một yếu tố khác thúc đẩy Trung Quốc quay lại thị trường là chi phí vận chuyển dầu bằng đường biển giảm mạnh. Cước vận chuyển trên tuyến từ Vịnh Oman tới Trung Quốc hiện vào khoảng 8 USD mỗi thùng, so với mức 21 USD chỉ 1 tháng trước. Như vậy, chi phí đã giảm khoảng 62%, giúp giá dầu thực tế khi đến các nhà máy lọc dầu Trung Quốc trở nên hấp dẫn hơn.

June Goh, nhà phân tích tại Sparta Commodities, cho rằng sự phục hồi của hoạt động nhập khẩu dầu thể hiện rõ nhất tại Trung Quốc. Các nước nhập khẩu lớn khác ở châu Á như Nhật Bản và Hàn Quốc trong vài tháng qua đã mua gần sát khả năng của họ, bất chấp giá dầu.

Trung Quốc lại ở vị thế khác, nước này là một trong số ít quốc gia nhập khẩu dầu lớn có khả năng giảm mạnh mua hàng từ thị trường quốc tế vào đầu năm, khi giá dầu tăng vọt sau khi eo biển Hormuz đóng cửa. Thay vì tiếp tục nhập khẩu với giá cao, Trung Quốc có thể rút dầu từ lượng dự trữ khổng lồ được tích lũy trước đó.

Ước tính, đến cuối năm 2025, Trung Quốc đã tích trữ khoảng 1,4 tỷ thùng dầu thô. Kho dự trữ được hình thành trong giai đoạn giá dầu thế giới thấp, đồng thời nước này có khả năng tiếp cận nguồn dầu Nga, Iran và Venezuela với mức chiết khấu.

Lượng dầu tích lũy này tạo ra vùng đệm lớn khi xung đột Trung Đông khiến nguồn cung và giá năng lượng biến động mạnh. Một số nhà phân tích thậm chí cho rằng việc Trung Quốc giảm nhu cầu mua dầu trên thị trường quốc tế trong thời điểm căng thẳng đã góp phần hạn chế một đợt tăng giá dầu toàn cầu nghiêm trọng hơn.

Tình thế hiện nay đang đảo chiều. Khi giá dầu, mức cộng của các loại dầu giao ngay và cước tàu cùng giảm, các nhà máy lọc dầu Trung Quốc bắt đầu quay lại thị trường để mua lượng lớn.

Việc Sinopec mua riêng 20 triệu thùng từ Tây Phi cho thấy tốc độ bổ sung nguồn cung đang diễn ra nhanh. Các lô dầu Trung Đông và Brazil đồng thời giúp doanh nghiệp Trung Quốc đa dạng hóa nguồn hàng trong lúc điều kiện thị trường thuận lợi hơn.

Trong khi đó, Trung Quốc trở lại thị trường với những đơn hàng lớn có thể tạo lực đỡ cho giá dầu thế giới, đồng thời thu hẹp lượng dầu giá rẻ đang sẵn có trên thị trường giao ngay và giúp hạ nhiệt cước vận tải.

title: Tác giả “Cha giàu, cha nghèo” cảnh báo khủng hoảng lớn hơn năm 2008 đã bắt đầu, tiết lộ 6 loại tài sản đang tích cực mua vào
description: Ông Robert Kiyosaki cảnh báo cuộc khủng hoảng kinh tế tiếp theo có thể nghiêm trọng hơn nhiều so với năm 2008, thậm chí đẩy thế giới vào một cuộc đại suy thoái.
content_md:
Ông Robert Kiyosaki cảnh báo cuộc khủng hoảng kinh tế tiếp theo có thể nghiêm trọng hơn nhiều so với năm 2008, thậm chí đẩy thế giới vào một cuộc đại suy thoái.

Trong bài đăng trên mạng xã hội X, Robert Kiyosaki - tác giả cuốn sách nổi tiếng “Cha giàu, cha nghèo” - nhắc lại cuộc khủng hoảng tài chính năm 2008 từng khiến Lehman Brothers sụp đổ và đẩy nền kinh tế toàn cầu đến bờ vực thẳm.

“Cuộc khủng hoảng mà chúng ta đang bước vào lớn hơn nhiều so với năm 2008. Đó có thể là một cuộc đại suy thoái toàn cầu”, ông Kiyosaki viết.

Vị tác giả cho rằng người dân Mỹ không nên trông chờ vào sự hỗ trợ của chính phủ để bảo vệ việc làm hay các khoản tiết kiệm hưu trí khi khủng hoảng xảy ra.

Ông Kiyosaki chỉ ra hàng loạt rủi ro, từ gánh nặng nợ ngày càng lớn, quy mô khổng lồ của thị trường phái sinh đến những khoản đầu tư liên quan đến thế chấp từng góp phần châm ngòi cho cuộc khủng hoảng năm 2008. Ông cũng dự báo một làn sóng in tiền quy mô lớn sắp bắt đầu.

“Cuộc in tiền quy mô lớn sắp bắt đầu. Năm 2026, Mỹ đang gánh khoản nợ 49.000 tỷ USD và con số này tiếp tục tăng. AI sẽ đe dọa nghiêm trọng sự ổn định của việc làm. Volkswagen vừa sa thải 100.000 lao động. Châu Âu đang chìm trong bất ổn”, ông viết.

Tuy nhiên, theo số liệu cập nhật của Bộ Tài chính Mỹ, nợ công nước này tính đến ngày 23/11 ở mức khoảng 40.710 tỷ USD, thấp hơn con số mà ông Kiyosaki đưa ra. Volkswagen cũng chưa sa thải 100.000 lao động mà mới công bố kế hoạch cắt giảm số lượng việc làm tương ứng vào cuối thập kỷ này hồi tháng 9.

Trước những rủi ro trên, tác giả “Cha giàu, cha nghèo” tiết lộ ông đang tăng cường mua vào 6 loại tài sản, gồm vàng, bạc, bitcoin, ethereum, bất động sản và dầu mỏ.

Ông Kiyosaki cho biết bản thân hy vọng dự báo của mình sẽ sai. Tuy nhiên, nếu cuộc khủng hoảng thực sự xảy ra như dự đoán, ông tin rằng một số tài sản đang nắm giữ có thể giúp mình gia nhập hàng ngũ những người siêu giàu.

*\*Bài viết chỉ thể hiện quan điểm của nhân vật được nhắc đến, không có giá trị khuyến nghị đầu tư.*

title: Đà Nẵng khởi công Cụm công nghiệp Hòa Nhơn gần 25ha
description: Ngày 25-11, UBND TP Đà Nẵng phối hợp Công ty Cổ phần Đầu tư Sài Gòn – Đà Nẵng (SDN) khởi công Dự án Cụm công nghiệp Hòa Nhơn tại xã Bà Nà.
content_md:
Ngày 25-11, UBND TP Đà Nẵng phối hợp Công ty Cổ phần Đầu tư Sài Gòn – Đà Nẵng (SDN) khởi công Dự án Cụm công nghiệp Hòa Nhơn tại xã Bà Nà.

Dự án có quy mô khoảng 24,75ha, trong đó diện tích đất thương phẩm hơn 15ha. Hệ thống hạ tầng kỹ thuật được định hướng đầu tư đồng bộ, hiện đại, phục vụ các ngành nghề như cơ khí, điện tử, thiết bị điện, chế biến, chế tạo và công nghiệp hỗ trợ.

Phát biểu tại buổi lễ, ông Phan Thái Bình, Phó Chủ tịch UBND TP Đà Nẵng cho biết, địa phương đang bước vào giai đoạn phát triển mới, với yêu cầu mở rộng không gian, nâng cao chất lượng tăng trưởng và tăng cường liên kết vùng. Trong đó, công nghiệp tiếp tục được xác định là một trong những động lực quan trọng.

Đà Nẵng định hướng ưu tiên phát triển công nghiệp công nghệ cao, công nghiệp số, chế biến, chế tạo và công nghiệp hỗ trợ theo hướng xanh, hiện đại, bền vững; đồng thời thúc đẩy các lĩnh vực vi mạch bán dẫn, trí tuệ nhân tạo, tự động hóa, vật liệu mới và năng lượng sạch, gắn với hệ thống logistics, cảng biển, sân bay và các trung tâm thương mại.

Việc đầu tư Cụm công nghiệp Hòa Nhơn có ý nghĩa thiết thực trong bổ sung không gian sản xuất, tạo cơ hội thu hút đầu tư và hỗ trợ doanh nghiệp địa phương, doanh nghiệp vừa và nhỏ mở rộng quy mô, đổi mới công nghệ, nâng cao năng suất, tham gia sâu hơn vào chuỗi cung ứng.

Lãnh đạo TP Đà Nẵng đề nghị chủ đầu tư tập trung nguồn lực, bảo đảm tiến độ, chất lượng công trình; hoàn thiện hạ tầng kỹ thuật, tuân thủ quy định về xây dựng, phòng cháy chữa cháy và bảo vệ môi trường. Đồng thời, cần công khai, minh bạch thông tin về giá thuê, tạo điều kiện để doanh nghiệp tiếp cận mặt bằng và chú trọng giải quyết việc làm cho người dân địa phương.

Các sở, ngành và UBND xã Bà Nà được đề nghị phối hợp, kịp thời tháo gỡ khó khăn, vướng mắc, tạo thuận lợi cho dự án triển khai đúng tiến độ.

Dịp này, SDN ký kết các thỏa thuận hợp tác với đối tác và trao quà hỗ trợ các hộ dân bị ảnh hưởng trong quá trình triển khai dự án.

title: Cổ phiếu tăng 60% từ đầu năm, một doanh nghiệp sắp tăng vốn gấp 2,7 lần, chia cổ tức tiền mặt 254%
description: Cổ đông sở hữu 1.000 cổ phiếu CLM dự kiến được nhận thêm gần 1.697 cổ phiếu mới. Doanh nghiệp này cũng chuẩn bị chi trả cổ tức bằng tiền mặt với tỷ lệ hơn 254%, cao nhất lịch sử hoạt động.
content_md:
Cổ đông sở hữu 1.000 cổ phiếu CLM dự kiến được nhận thêm gần 1.697 cổ phiếu mới. Doanh nghiệp này cũng chuẩn bị chi trả cổ tức bằng tiền mặt với tỷ lệ hơn 254%, cao nhất lịch sử hoạt động.

CTCP Xuất nhập khẩu Than - Vinacomin (Coalimex, HNX: CLM) vừa công bố nghị quyết Đại hội đồng cổ đông (ĐHĐCĐ) bất thường năm 2026, thông qua phương án tăng vốn điều lệ và điều chỉnh kế hoạch phân phối lợi nhuận năm 2025.

Theo đó, Coalimex dự kiến phát hành hơn 24,5 triệu cổ phiếu thưởng cho cổ đông hiện hữu với tỷ lệ gần 170%. Toàn bộ cổ phiếu phát hành thêm không bị hạn chế chuyển nhượng.

Nguồn vốn thực hiện được lấy từ thặng dư vốn cổ phần và quỹ đầu tư phát triển tại báo cáo tài chính năm 2025 đã kiểm toán. Sau khi hoàn tất phát hành, vốn điều lệ của Coalimex sẽ tăng gấp 2,7 lần, từ gần 145 tỷ đồng lên hơn 390 tỷ đồng.

Song song với kế hoạch tăng vốn, cổ đông Coalimex cũng thông qua phương án trả cổ tức tiền mặt bổ sung năm 2025 với tỷ lệ hơn 254%, tương ứng mỗi cổ phiếu được nhận khoảng 25.409 đồng. Với gần 14,5 triệu cổ phiếu đang lưu hành, doanh nghiệp dự kiến chi gần 368 tỷ đồng cho đợt thanh toán này.

Tập đoàn Công nghiệp Than - Khoáng sản Việt Nam (TKV), cổ đông lớn nhất của Coalimex với tỷ lệ sở hữu 55,41% vốn điều lệ, dự kiến thu về khoảng 204 tỷ đồng.

Trước đó, Coalimex đã triển khai phương án trả cổ tức năm 2025 với tỷ lệ 30% bằng tiền mặt và 31,5% bằng cổ phiếu. Với phương án bổ sung vừa được thông qua, tổng số tiền chi trả cổ tức năm 2025 sẽ vượt 400 tỷ đồng. Đây cũng là đợt thưởng cổ phiếu và trả cổ tức bằng tiền mặt có tỷ lệ cao nhất kể từ khi doanh nghiệp đi vào hoạt động.

**CỔ PHIẾU TĂNG MẠNH, LỢI NHUẬN PHỤC HỒI**

Trên thị trường chứng khoán, cổ phiếu CLM ghi nhận đà tăng mạnh trong giai đoạn tháng 10-11/2026, từ vùng giá 50.000 đồng/cổ phiếu lên trên 80.000 đồng/cổ phiếu.

Kết thúc phiên giao dịch ngày 25/11, CLM dừng ở mức 76.000 đồng/cổ phiếu, tăng 60% kể từ đầu năm. Vốn hóa thị trường của Coalimex đạt gần 1.100 tỷ đồng. Thanh khoản của mã cổ phiếu này khá thấp, bình quân chỉ đạt 819 đơn vị mỗi phiên từ đầu năm.

Về kết quả kinh doanh, sau ba năm liên tiếp ghi nhận lợi nhuận sụt giảm, Coalimex đang cho thấy sự phục hồi trong năm 2026. Lũy kế 9 tháng đầu năm, doanh nghiệp đạt doanh thu thuần hơn 15.864 tỷ đồng, tăng 11% so với cùng kỳ. Lợi nhuận sau thuế đạt gần 76 tỷ đồng, tăng 23% và đã nhỉnh hơn kết quả thực hiện cả năm 2025.

Coalimex được thành lập năm 1982, chuyển sang mô hình công ty cổ phần vào năm 2004 với vốn điều lệ ban đầu 20 tỷ đồng. Doanh nghiệp chính thức niêm yết cổ phiếu trên HNX vào tháng 4/2016.

Coalimex không phải doanh nghiệp duy nhất thuộc hệ sinh thái TKV triển khai kế hoạch tăng vốn và chia cổ tức tỷ lệ cao trong thời gian gần đây. Trước đó, CTCP Kinh doanh Than Miền Bắc - Vinacomin (HNX: TMB) cũng công bố phương án phát hành 27,45 triệu cổ phiếu, nâng vốn điều lệ lên gần 425 tỷ đồng, đồng thời trả cổ tức tiền mặt với tỷ lệ hơn 241%. Cổ phiếu TMB từng ghi nhận mức tăng 74% chỉ trong khoảng một tháng.
